licences.MIT: Permissive (Expat). The FSF lists it as compatible with the GNU GPL.
licences.ISC: Permissive. The FSF lists it as compatible with the GNU GPL.
licences.0BSD: Permissive with no conditions at all, so nothing in it can conflict with the AGPL.
licences.BSD-2-Clause: Permissive (FreeBSD licence). The FSF lists it as compatible with the GNU GPL.
licences.BSD-3-Clause: Permissive (modified BSD licence). The FSF lists it as compatible with the GNU GPL.
licences.Apache-2.0: Permissive. The FSF lists it as compatible with GPL version 3, and so with AGPL version 3.
licences.Zlib: Permissive. The FSF lists it as compatible with the GNU GPL.
licences.PSF-2.0: Python Software Foundation licence. The FSF lists Python 2.0.1 and later licences as compatible with the GNU GPL.
licences.CC0-1.0: Public domain dedication with a permissive fallback. The FSF lists it as compatible with the GNU GPL.
licences.MPL-2.0: Weak copyleft. Section 3.3 allows combining with the GNU GPL and AGPL unless the code is marked "Incompatible With Secondary Licenses"; check for that notice when adding a direct MPL dependency.
licences.LGPL-2.1-or-later: Weak copyleft, usable under LGPL 3, which the FSF lists as compatible with GPL 3.
licences.LGPL-3.0-only: Weak copyleft. The FSF lists it as compatible with GPL 3.
licences.LGPL-3.0-or-later: Weak copyleft. The FSF lists it as compatible with GPL 3.
licences.GPL-2.0-or-later: Usable under GPL 3, which section 13 of the AGPL allows combining with.
licences.GPL-3.0-only: Section 13 of AGPL 3 and of GPL 3 allows combining the two.
licences.GPL-3.0-or-later: Section 13 of AGPL 3 and of GPL 3 allows combining the two.
licences.AGPL-3.0-only: Same licence as Off Book, at version 3.
